issues.summary: The no-recovery recoil branch self-anchors instead of reaching the contractually required attributable failure.
reproduction: Open build ac856b2dc221c666ec8ab25874a9cfd43df8b949a7b382b291f7229fbba092ac at 1180x720 and load the recoil-wall acceptance scenario after natural play.
Observe the initial real-time handle bounce from recoil-wall: normalX=-1 and player vx=-201.6.
Provide no mouse input for 2.8 seconds.
Observe handle/body bounces from under-slat and side-tag followed by an edge anchor to recoil-wall; status=anchored and failReason=null. Compare recoil-before.png and recoil-no-recovery.png.
Control branch: reload the scenario, make one real mouse click immediately, and after 120ms observe vx=8.4, vy=-335 plus flip/cut feedback.
issues.expected: Without the timely recovery click, the negative recoil branch should end in a clearly attributable gap or hazard failure; with the click, the player should visibly recover.
issues.actual: The timely click does reverse the immediate recoil, but the no-input branch safely settles into an edge anchor after 2.8s and therefore does not demonstrate the required pressure/failure consequence.

issues.summary: The dualRole structure disappears after cutting, but its pre-cut support/anchoring behavior is not independently reachable with stable real input.
reproduction: At 1180x720 load the dual-role acceptance scenario after natural play and confirm dual-bridge-face active=true and dual-bridge cut=false/solid=true.
Use real mouse launch plus follow-up timing offsets of 0,20,40,60,80,100,120,220,320 and 420ms.
Every tested branch produces a tip cut of dual-bridge; none produces anchorId=dual-bridge-face.
Repeat from the normal course with a visible-state input policy through x>1600; the structure is again cut and the face deactivates without a pre-cut anchor.
issues.expected: At least one clear, repeatable real-input branch should land on and anchor to the intact dualRole support before another branch cuts it away.
issues.actual: The post-cut disappearance is proven, but no pre-cut support contact was reproduced in the acceptance scenario or a normal-course attempt, leaving DUAL-001 unverified.
